title: Botched install caused installer to stop because it thinks it is installed.
summary: The installer reports 0x81f40001 after a broken uninstall, but the evidence now overlaps the active cross-scope installer deadlock tracker.
next_action: Draft a duplicate-handling comment that points the reporter to the active installer deadlock thread and known workaround history.

confidence.rationale: The error string, current installer conditions, and open tracker all line up with the same cross-scope detection family.

judgment.rationale: The failure matches the open installer deadlock tracked in Issue 43774 and the closely related Issue 47250 workaround discussion.
evidence: The reporter quotes installer error 0x81f40001 saying PowerToys is already installed for all users.
Issue 47250 documented the same cross-scope uninstall/repair block and tied it to PowerToysSetupVNext conditions.
The current installer source in installer/PowerToysSetupVNext/PowerToys.wxs still contains the cross-scope guard without the WixBundleInstalled escape on the first condition.
judgment.recommended_action: Route this issue to the canonical installer deadlock tracker instead of creating a separate design thread here.

fix_assessment.rationale: The product bug is already tracked elsewhere; a duplicate fix plan here would split the history and workaround guidance.

issue_context.summary: The reporter wants to reinstall after a botched uninstall, but the installer still claims PowerToys is already installed for all users.
known_information: The issue is against PowerToys 0.100.2-x64 installed from GitHub.
The reporter cannot currently reinstall any version and explicitly asked whether there is a registry or cleanup route.
The issue still carries Needs-Author-Feedback, but the underlying installer family already has active tracking elsewhere.
inferences: This is likely the same cross-scope installer state deadlock rather than a brand-new install surface.
The most useful maintainer action is dedupe/navigation, not another generic request for steps the reporter cannot recreate.
issue_context.analysis: Because the reporter mainly needs the known fix/workaround path and the underlying bug family is already open elsewhere, the artifact should steer maintainers to consolidate rather than restart diagnosis from scratch.
initial_investigation: Issue 43774 is still open for this installer deadlock family.
Issue 47250 includes a detailed root-cause explanation and workaround discussion for the same 0x81f40001 condition.
installer/PowerToysSetupVNext/PowerToys.wxs still shows the cross-scope condition that can block uninstall/repair paths.

comment.body: Thanks for the extra detail. This appears to match the active installer deadlock family tracked in Issue 43774, with closely related workaround history in Issue 47250: the bundle detects the opposite install scope and then blocks uninstall or reinstall with error 0x81f40001. I would route this thread there instead of starting a separate fix path here, so the workaround steps and eventual installer fix stay consolidated in one place.
